title: ES Security Assistant Model Runtime guide uses default-on and opt-in wording
problem: The release guide describes Model Runtime as default for ES 8.6 and later and uses opt-in wording in its usage section. It does not explain whether those descriptions refer to the same deployment or initial setting.

products: Splunk Security Assistant in Enterprise Security
versions: ES 8.6+ as named in the guide
audiences: Readers evaluating Security Assistant model-processing boundaries
exclusions: Actual deployment defaults, tenant policy, SAIA Agent Mode, SOC workflow runtime, data residency, entitlement and regulated authorization.

scopeComparison: The default-setting statement and usage wording are in separate subsections of the same versioned release guide. Neither establishes a setting for a specific tenant or service offering.

impact.customerScenario: A reader evaluating whether Security Assistant prompts may be sent beyond the Splunk platform boundary.
impact.consequence: Confirm the applicable configuration and policy before relying on the documentation for default behavior or processing location.

confidence.rationale: Exact public source sections establish a wording ambiguity. No tenant configuration was inspected.

lifecycle.reason: Exact deployment defaults and configuration-specific semantics remain unresolved.

evidence.section: Model Runtime in Splunk Security Assistant > What it means when you let Splunk determine the best model to use
evidence.statement: The guide states that ES 8.6 and later use Model Runtime by default and describes the administrator control for Splunk-hosted models only.
